research_question: Can the preregistered divergence-free Gaussian SST vortex pressure model reproduce a Newtonian microgravity force gradient and material mass without fitting G or a phenomenological source-to-mass map?
objective: Separate article-derived Newton benchmark, numerical Euler-Poisson solver qualification and source-independent SST mechanisms.
null_hypothesis: The concrete Gaussian local-vortex closure fails source mass or r^-2 scaling and has no independently identified SST constant.
alternative_hypothesis: A pre-registered SST pressure and mass closure passes absolute magnitude, mass scaling and r^-2 force scaling without fit.
assumptions: 3D incompressible inviscid Euler snapshot, no external body-force
Gaussian swirling localized velocity field is a restricted candidate, not generic SST
finite field width a=3 mm is an unverified coarse graining of a femtometre core
pressure acting on a small test sphere is approximated by -V grad p at the centre
public article observations are validation benchmarks but cannot constitute target-blind discovery

observables.definition: source energy mass / observed physical mass

steps.operation: integrate pressure source on midpoint grid, refine resolution

falsification_criteria.criterion: source mass closure predicted to agree within 10% without fit
far-field force slope must be within 0.2 of 2

edge_cases: r close to a outside point-test approximation
source and test not rigid vortices
published force sensitivity derived partly from Newton baseline
predictions: Gaussian pressure multipole force decreases faster than inverse square
Energy-mass mismatch under fixed coarse graining
